summary: Chamath argues the antitrust ruling removes enormous downside risk for Google, freeing it to compete aggressively in AI without internal/external drag, and that the free market is already doing the job of forcing competition.
quote: The great news for Google is that this takes an enormous risk off the table. And now I think that they probably have even more ambition and energy to just go for it and try to compete.

summary: Sacks argues Google faces an existential threat to its core search business as users shift to AI chatbots, with ~90% of AI revenue going to OpenAI and multiple competitive AI players challenging its dominant position.
quote: Google for the first time in a long while is existentially threatened by what's happened with AI. I mean, their cash cow, the core of their business is search, and people are starting to substitute in droves from traditional Google
